clue.text: Is numb, I suspect, in exploration vessel

indicators.note: as an adjective, suspect means dubious or not genuine, so the letters before it are not to be trusted in their given order

parts.note: the letters of these three words, punctuation ignored

explanation.surface: Someone numb with cold suspects they are aboard a research vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A minisub is a small submarine, typically used for undersea exploration and research.

clue.text: Provided in most new designs

indicators.note: in puts one word inside the other
new means made afresh, so the combined letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
if means provided that

explanation.surface: Fresh designs are provided in the majority of cases.
explanation.definitionFit: A motif is a recurring decorative pattern or design element.

clue.text: Admiral in hold

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Horatio, the admiral killed at Trafalgar
second meaning: a wrestling grip on the neck from behind

explanation.surface: An admiral sits down in a ship's hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold' suggests a ship's cargo space; it is the wrestling hold.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelson is Britain's naval hero and also a wrestling grip, as in a full nelson.

clue.text: Show violence towards powerful member

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to coerce someone by force

explanation.surface: An influential committee member is being bullied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' reads as a person in a club; here it is a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to bully physically, and the phrase literally is a muscular limb.

clue.text: Items of cutlery in trunk, best I've touched

indicators.note: touched can mean slightly crazy, so the letters go haywire

parts.note: the letters of all three words, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone's finest cutlery is packed in a trunk they have handled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touched' looks like handled; it is the informal sense of mildly mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Butter knives are blunt knives for spreading, a kind of table cutlery.

clue.text: Practise in heat

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to loosen up or rehearse before an event
second meaning: to make something warmer, as with leftovers

explanation.surface: An athlete trains during a qualifying round of a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heat' looks like a qualifying race, which fits the practise picture, but here it is a verb meaning make warmer.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb covers both pre-exercise limbering and reheating food or a room.

clue.text: Boy in short anorak, wound up

indicators.note: something wound up is twisted round, so the remaining letters change their order
short means cut off before the end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A boy wears a cropped anorak and is in a state of agitation.
explanation.definitionFit: Aaron is a male given name, and crosswords use boy for any male name.

clue.text: Boatman drifting round one Canadian lake

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the rearranged letters enclose the numeral
drifting means moving aimlessly, so the letters wander out of order

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A boatman drifts around a lake in Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Manitoba is a large lake in the Canadian province of the same name.

clue.text: Legendary bird in part of Arizona

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the mythical bird reborn from its ashes
second meaning: the state capital of Arizona

explanation.surface: A mythical bird is sighted in the Arizona desert.
explanation.definitionFit: The phoenix of myth rises from its own ashes; the city is Arizona's capital.

clue.text: Suffer later, toe broken

indicators.note: something broken has its parts scattered, so the letters are reassembled in a fresh order

parts.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: Someone with a broken toe will be in pain later on.
explanation.definitionFit: Suffer in its older sense means allow or put up with, as in 'suffer fools gladly'.

clue.text: Drunk on port? At once!

indicators.note: a drunk person staggers about, so the letters reel into a new order

parts.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: Someone tipsy on port demands something be done immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: Pronto is an informal borrowing from Spanish and Italian for immediately or without delay.

clue.text: Place for opera — NY one burgled, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately signals things going wrong, so the letters end up in disarray

parts.note: the letters of all three words

explanation.surface: A New York opera house was regrettably broken into.
explanation.walkthrough: Glyndebourne is a country house in Sussex, England, home to a famous summer opera festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Glyndebourne is an English opera house and festival venue in East Sussex.

clue.text: Loud argument with knight makes one scowl

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
a row is a noisy quarrel
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A noisy quarrel with a knight leaves someone glowering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loud argument' reads as one idea, but loud is its own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To frown and to scowl are both verbs for furrowing the brow in displeasure.

clue.text: Duke, duke wife ignored

indicators.note: what is ignored is left out, so the letter for the wife is dropped

parts.note: the Duke of Wellington, victor at Waterloo
w is the standard abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A duke whose wife is snubbed by society.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing W from WELLINGTON leaves ELLINGTON: one duke turns into another.
explanation.definitionFit: Duke Ellington was the American jazz bandleader and composer, Duke being his nickname.

clue.text: Sailor giving evidence? He may spring a surprise

parts.note: jack, or Jack Tar, is slang for a sailor
a witness giving evidence stands in the witness box

explanation.surface: A seaman testifying in court may say something unexpected.
explanation.definitionFit: The toy figure leaps out on a spring when its lid opens, startling whoever opens it.

clue.text: Golfing feat in difficult situation, popular on last in game?

parts.note: to be in a hole is to be in trouble
in means popular, fashionable
taken as written

indicators.note: last in a word means its final letter only

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A golfer achieves a great shot while in trouble in the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Holing the ball with a single stroke from the tee is a golfer's rare ace.

clue.text: Notice alternative selection

parts.note: an ad, advertisement, is a notice
an option is an alternative choice

explanation.surface: A notice lists a different choice to pick from.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoption is the act of choosing and taking up something, such as a candidate or policy.

clue.text: French governess forced one to go in river

parts.note: made someone do it means forced them

indicators.note: going in means being placed inside, so the single letter sits within the river's name

parts.note: the Moselle flows through France, Luxembourg and Germany
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A governess in France was made to go into a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Mademoiselle, the French title for an unmarried woman, was once used in Britain for a French governess.

clue.text: Bad hearing the second I popped out in wind?

indicators.note: what has popped out is gone, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a mistrial is a trial invalidated by error
the second of the two Is in the word

explanation.surface: Someone with poor hearing missed a moment because of wind noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' suggests listening; it is a court hearing. 'The second' looks like a moment of time, but it picks the second I.
explanation.definitionFit: The mistral is a strong cold northerly wind in southern France.

clue.text: Friend entertaining the Spanish with a rice dish they like?

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to hold them in your home, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a pal is a friend
el is Spanish for 'the'
taken as written

explanation.surface: A friend hosts some Spaniards with a rice dish they enjoy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They' refers back to the Spanish: the question mark admits the definition leans on the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Paella is the saffron rice dish of Valencia, a favourite in Spain.

clue.text: Awful smell coming from small fish

parts.note: s is the abbreviation for small
the tench is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A rank odour comes off a little fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A stench is a strong, foul odour, a stink.

clue.text: Comic strip character, perhaps getting petrol on her overalls, initially?

parts.note: super is a high-octane grade of petrol
her taken as written, placed after the petrol

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word just before it

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A cartoon heroine spills fuel on her work clothes at the garage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' means the following piece comes after the petrol. Super is premium-grade petrol in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Superman and Batman are examples of the costumed caped crusaders found in comic strips.

clue.text: Check about first of Georges to rule as monarch

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain

indicators.note: first of points to the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the opening letter of the name

explanation.surface: A historian examines the record of the Georges who ruled as kings.
explanation.definitionFit: To reign is to hold royal power and occupy the throne.

clue.text: Out of place down in Italy

indicators.note: in places one element inside the other, here within the country's abbreviation

parts.note: IT is the international code for Italy
nap is the soft fuzzy surface of fabric, like down

explanation.surface: Someone feels like a fish out of water while feeling low in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down' suggests feeling sad, but it is the fluffy kind, matching the raised pile called nap.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means unsuitable or inappropriate, fitting badly where it is placed.

clue.text: Artist is at home portraying dried fruit

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician
taken as written
in means at home

explanation.surface: A painter works at home on a still life of dried fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A raisin is a grape that has been dried, sold as a common dried fruit.

clue.text: In New York City borough, see tailless cat by stream

indicators.note: without a tail means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a brook is a small stream
the lynx is a wild cat

explanation.surface: A sightseer in New York spots a bobtailed cat beside a creek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' only says the two are side by side; the stream comes first. A lynx naturally has a stubby tail, which makes 'tailless' apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Brooklyn is one of the five boroughs making up New York City.

clue.text: Heather describing trendy piece of waistcoat material

indicators.note: to describe can mean to trace a line around, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: ling is a common heather
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: A sprig of heather adorns a fashionable bit of waistcoat fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a woman's name; it is the plant, called ling.
explanation.definitionFit: The lining is the inner layer of fabric sewn inside a garment such as a waistcoat.

clue.text: Rot shown in elm, primarily, and two other types of tree

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is wanted

parts.note: the first letter of the tree

parts.words: and two other types of tree
parts.note: yew is one tree

parts.words: and two other types of tree
parts.note: ash is the other tree

explanation.surface: Decay has appeared in an elm and two further trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rot' suggests tree decay, which suits the surface, but it means nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyewash is informal for nonsense or humbug, just as rot is.
